knowledge:
- key_parameters: file1=Path to input file containing mate 1 reads or single-ended reads ;; file2=Path to input file containing mate 2 reads ;; basename=Default prefix for all output files generated by AdapterRemoval ;; adapter1=Adapter sequence expected to be found in mate 1 reads ;; adapter2=Adapter sequence expected to be found in mate 2 reads ;; references=Character vector of FASTA reference file paths for index building ;; bt2Index=Prefix of the Bowtie2 index to be built or used ;; output=Output file path for alignment results ;; outputType=Format of alignment output, such as "sam" ;; seq1=Preprocessed mate 1 reads file path for alignment ;; seq2=Preprocessed mate 2 reads file path for alignment ;; overwrite=Logical indicating whether to overwrite existing files
- alternatives: None mentioned, though Bowtie2 is specifically noted as being optimized for aligning reads with lengths above 50bp.
- when_to_use: Use this package when you have raw high-throughput sequencing reads (FASTQ format) that require adapter trimming or merging, followed by alignment to a reference genome (FASTA format) to produce SAM/BAM files.
- pitfalls: Single-end data is not supported for automatic adapter identification via identify_adapters; adapter sequences must be known beforehand for single-end data. Bowtie2 indexes are not compatible with Bowtie1. Runs are not deterministic if more than one thread is used during collapsing. Bowtie2 requires a 64-bit R environment.

workflows.name: adapter_trimming_and_alignment
workflows.intent: Preprocess raw paired-end sequencing reads by identifying and removing adapters, building a Bowtie2 index, and aligning the trimmed reads to the reference genome.
workflows.stages: 1. Identify adapter sequences from raw paired-end reads using identify_adapters ;; 2. Trim identified adapters from reads using remove_adapters ;; 3. Build a Bowtie2 index from reference FASTA files using bowtie2_build ;; 4. Align the trimmed reads to the reference index using bowtie2_samtools to generate a SAM file
workflows.code:
td <- tempdir()
reads_1 <- system.file(package="Rbowtie2", "extdata", "adrm", "reads_1.fq")
reads_2 <- system.file(package="Rbowtie2", "extdata", "adrm", "reads_2.fq")
(adapters <- 
    identify_adapters(file1=reads_1,file2=reads_2,
                      basename=file.path(td,"reads"),
                      "--threads 3",overwrite=TRUE))
(cmdout<-remove_adapters(file1=reads_1,file2=reads_2,adapter1 = adapters[1], 
                adapter2 = adapters[2],
output1=file.path(td,"reads_1.trimmed.fq"),
output2=file.path(td,"reads_2.trimmed.fq"),
basename=file.path(td,"reads.base"),overwrite=TRUE,"--threads 3"))
td <- tempdir()
refs <- dir(system.file(package="Rbowtie2", "extdata", "bt2","refs"),full=TRUE)
(cmdout<-bowtie2_build(references=refs, 
              bt2Index=file.path(td, "lambda_virus"), "--threads 4 --quiet",
              overwrite=TRUE))
reads_1 <- system.file(package="Rbowtie2", "extdata", 
                       "bt2", "reads", "reads_1.fastq")
reads_2 <- system.file(package="Rbowtie2", "extdata", 
                       "bt2", "reads", "reads_2.fastq")
if(file.exists(file.path(td, "lambda_virus.1.bt2"))){
    (cmdout<-bowtie2_samtools(bt2Index = file.path(td, "lambda_virus"),
        output = file.path(td, "result"),
        outputType = "sam",
        seq1=reads_1,
        seq2=reads_2,
        overwrite=TRUE,
        bamFile = NULL,
        "--threads 3"))
    head(readLines(file.path(td, "result.sam")))
}
